expected_output.reasoning:
The investigation correctly identified that the discrepancy is due to client-side/application-side factors rather than Bedrock inference itself. It explicitly ruled out the Bedrock service getting slower (flat ms/output-token, no throttles/errors, no config changes) and instead pointed to: (1) a traffic-mix shift explaining the account-wide metric change, and (2) a shift to tool_use loops meaning each app-level request now spans multiple Converse calls plus tool execution and client/network time, none of which is captured by the per-call InvocationLatency metric. This directly matches the expected root cause that the gap is explained by time spent outside Bedrock's measured service-side path (multiple calls per request, client-side orchestration/tool execution overhead) rather than inference slowing down. The investigation explicitly frames the measurement-boundary discrepancy (InvocationLatency is per-call server-side only) as the decisive evidence, consistent with the expected answer, even though it attributes the extra client-side time specifically to tool-use loop multiplication rather than connection pooling/retries/payload growth. This is a reasonable and specific identification of a client-side cause for the measurement gap, fulfilling the core expectation that the regression is located outside Bedrock's own inference path and tied to the measurement boundary.</reasoning>
